What is a Controller?

A Controller is a coordinating authority within the pipeline. Controllers do not transform state or produce values. Instead, they mediate, arbitrate, and finalize control decisions that affect how pipeline execution proceeds.

Controllers operate across pipeline stages rather than within a single stage. They observe requests emitted by Behaviors, apply centralized decision logic, and issue authoritative outcomes that determine whether execution execution buffers, retries, completes successfully, denies progression, or fails with error.

Controllers are never implicitly enabled. A Controller participates in a FeatureCell pipeline only if it is explicitly registered during FeatureCell configuration. If a required Controller is omitted, the pipeline will fail fast rather than execute with incomplete authority.

When a FeatureCell is configured, validates each registered Controller and integrates it into the pipeline’s coordination layer. Controllers do not invoke Behaviors directly, and Behaviors do not coordinate with one another. All cross-cutting decisions flow through Controllers.

This separation ensures that control flow, arbitration, and policy enforcement are centralized, explicit, and deterministic—rather than being distributed across individual Behaviors.

There are no Core Controllers. Instead, a single Decision Engine is always present and coordinates all registered Controllers. Because Controllers may be stacked, the Decision Engine serves as the authoritative coordination layer. All other Controllers are optional add-on controllers and participate in the pipeline only when explicitly included in the FeatureCell definition.

Note

Controllers are not required for a FeatureCell to store, update, or emit state. A FeatureCell can operate correctly using only Behaviors and the core pipeline. Controllers are introduced only when additional coordination, arbitration, or policy enforcement is required.

Controller Anatomy

Every Controller conforms to a strict contract so it can safely coordinate pipeline execution.

Because all Controllers follow this contract, they can operate independently of the Behaviors that rely on them. A Controller does not need to know which Behavior emitted a request—only how to arbitrate the decision it represents.

Addon Controllers

There are only add-on Controllers in the pipeline.

Addon Controllers

  • Optional, engineer-selected Controllers registered during FeatureCell configuration.
  • Addon Controllers may be sourced from extension packages (such as /addons) or implemented directly by engineers.
  • Provide centralized coordination for cross-cutting concerns such as stepwise policy enforcement, external approvals, multi-stage gating, or deferred execution.
  • Do not mutate state or emit snapshots; they only issue authoritative control decisions.

This separation ensures that control authority is explicit and centralized, while allowing FeatureCells to opt into additional coordination models when required.

Why Controllers Matter

Controllers are what allow pipelines to remain deterministic even when control logic spans multiple stages or asynchronous boundaries:

  • Authoritative — Controllers are the single source of truth for pipeline control decisions.
  • Centralized — Complex coordination logic is not scattered across Behaviors.
  • Deterministic — Decisions are serialized, validated, and finalized in one place.
  • Safe — Pipelines fail fast if required Controllers are missing or misconfigured.

Understanding Controllers is essential for advanced FeatureCell pipelines, as they define how enforces policy, arbitration, and execution safety.

Controller–Behavior Dependency

Some Controllers are designed to coordinate or arbitrate one or more specific Behaviors. When such a dependency exists, both the Controller and its corresponding Behavior must be included in the FeatureCell declaration.

Registering a dependent Behavior without its required Controller—or registering a Controller without the Behavior it coordinates—results in an invalid FeatureCell configuration and causes pipeline initialization to fail.

does not implicitly enable Controllers or Behaviors. All dependencies must be declared explicitly to ensure deterministic execution, correct arbitration, and enforcement of policy boundaries.

Pipeline

Controllers operate within the Conductor to coordinate pipeline execution rather than transform data. Behaviors emit execution requests; Controllers arbitrate and resolve them.

Example
{{`// app.config.ts
provideFeatureCell(
  EmployeeService,
  {
    key: 'employees',
    initialState: [] 
  },
  [
    // opt-in behavior array 
    withStepwiseResolveBehavior
  ],
  [
    // opt-in controller array 
    withStepwiseController
  ]
);

// employee.service.ts
this.vault.withStepwiseResolve(
  stepwiseCallback: fn
).initialize()`}}
 
{{`export const employeeCell = FeatureCell(
  EmployeeCell, 
  {
    key: 'employees',
    initialState: [] 
  },
  [
    // opt-in behavior array 
    withStepwiseResolveBehavior
  ],
  [
    // opt-in controller array 
    withStepwiseController
  ]
);

employeeCell.withStepwiseResolve(
  stepwiseCallback: fn
).initialize() `}}
